query: measured latency cost of methods for Publish the stage-2 inlier-face width, height, and depth in metres on /pps/pallet_pose_rich with the pose from that same estimate. Width is the camera-x span of the inlier face, height is the camera-y span, and depth is the mean range. The vehicle's dynamic handling process can then size the pallet from the pose it is about to use while the scene can still change. on src
findings: Camera-x span and camera-y span are one axis-aligned pass over the stage-2 inliers, and mean range is one extra sum in that same pass. Dimitrov, Holst, Knauer, and Kriegel (GRAPP 2008, C++, Core Duo 2.33 GHz) measured that pass at 0.624 ms for 10,000 points and 16.6 ms for the Lucy set (262,909 vertices). Discrete PCA on those same sets took 36.0 ms and 236 ms. A minimum-volume search took seconds. PCA and an oriented box are a different quantity from the camera-axis span, and they cost about 14× to 58× the axis-aligned pass.

Calling pcl::getMinMax3D after copying inliers into a PCL cloud was about 15× slower than a scalar min/max loop on multi-megabyte XYZ clouds (10-trial average). The PCL moment-of-inertia tutorial says to use getMinMax3D for an axis-aligned box and computeCentroidAndOBB for an oriented box. A 3D centroid is a second sweep and is not the mean range this feature asks for.

Three float64 fields on the existing /pps/pallet_pose_rich message sit where ROS 2 latency does not move with payload. Kronauer, Pohlmann, Matthé, Meissner, and Fettweis (2021, ROS 2 Foxy, localhost UDP, i7-8700 and Raspberry Pi 4) measured the same latency at 128 B, 1 KB, and 10 KB; it rose only at 100 KB and 500 KB, past the 64 KB UDP fragment. At 128 B, ROS 2 added up to 50% over raw DDS, and that gap was notification delay. Fast DDS CDR of a geometry_msgs/Pose is 14.9 ns and of a Vector3 is 9.5 ns (rosidl_typesupport_fastrtps PR 150, mean of three runs, pinned core), so three extra doubles are nanoseconds of serialize time.

A second topic pays another full hop. Same-process ROS 2 C++ P90 per hop on an i7-9700K was 113 µs at 100 Hz and 138 µs at 1 kHz for a small message (Yu, ROS2-pubsub-benchmark). Publishing the inlier cloud so the vehicle computes the size itself is the large-payload path: Nishikawa et al. (arXiv:2506.16882, Humble, Cyclone DDS, separate processes) measured PointCloud2 latency growing with size, and an Autoware megabyte-scale cloud topic at 64.5 ms average (99.5 ms max) before a zero-copy change. String diagnostics are the other costly attach path: ROS 2 DDS tuning notes that arrays of non-primitives, including builtin_interfaces/Time and strings, stall publish(), while the same Fast DDS microbenchmark serializes a trivial String in 10.7 ns but a nested Marker in 394 ns.
